newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican soldier dies in clash with armed group.
newsitem.headline: Mexican soldier dies in clash with armed group.

text.p: A Mexican soldier died on Tuesday in a clash between the military and a group of unknown gunmen in the southwestern state of Guerrero, the military said.

About 25 armed men attacked a unit of troops carrying out routine anti-drugs operations in the municipality of Atoyac de Alvarez, some 40 miles (62 km) northwest of this Pacific tourist resort, the military said in a statement.
It was not clear whether the gunmen were members of a drugs gang or belonged to the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR), a Marxist guerrilla group that made its debut in the Atoyac area in June 1996.
"Part of a permanent reconnaissance mission against narco-traffickers was attacked with firearms by a group of about 25 armed men," the statement said.

At least two soldiers and two rebels were killed last weekend in a clash between the EPR and army troops in Guerrero, one of Mexico's poorest states. The EPR claimed on Monday that at least 30 troops were killed or wounded in the fight.

Three helicopters and two small aircraft flew over the area minutes after Tuesday's attack, which lasted for about 20 minutes, according to local residents. Truckloads of troops also combed the area in search of the gunmen.
"We were prohibited from leaving our homes and we heard volleys of gunfire," Roberto Hernandez, a local schoolteacher, told Reuters in a telephone interview from the nearby community of El Quemado.

The EPR, which has called for the overthrow of Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo's government, had been relatively quiet this year until last weekend's battle. The group claimed on Monday that increased hostilities by troops were forcing the guerrillas to defend themselves.
